result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers recommend explicit modes, with Select as the default, undo for Paint and a deliberate step for Record. B fits this operator more closely: it states its assumptions about a volunteer in a dim booth, gives a more concrete design for Record (naming the target cue, confirming only on overwrite, keeping past versions recoverable) and asks whether painting changes the stage lights immediately. A names the cost of modes more directly, but its advice is a bit more generic. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both recommend explicit modes and keep Record deliberate and separate. A ties its advice more closely to the booth: it states its operator assumptions, raises the live-versus-blind paint question that most affects show-time risk, keeps a persistent Undo rather than a toast, and keeps old cue versions so even an overwrite can be rolled back. B is tighter and openly names the cost of its own choice (mode errors), and its show-time lock is a good idea, but some points such as accessibility are more generic, and A's opening 'two or three' modes is only a slight hedge.
